messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

The game works, and now we want prizes.

The quiz settings get a new field, "Number of winners" (a number, at least 1, 3 by default).

Scoring:

- Each correct answer gives one point.
- Players with equal points are ranked by speed: the total time of their correct answers wins when it is lower. The time of an answer runs from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick.
- Players don't see points during the game.

Speed now decides ties, so all players must get each question at the same moment: the big screen and the phones must follow the moderator close to instantly.

After "End quiz":

- The big screen shows the leaderboard: one list item for each player, in order, with the place, the name, and the points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points").
- Each player's phone shows the place ("Place 2 of 5") and the points ("3 points").

Picking the winners (N is the number of winners):

- The "Top N" button (for example, "Top 3") makes the first N players of the leaderboard the winners.
- The "Draw" button is for ties. Every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed doesn't matter here). Each click draws again.
- Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
- The "Reset winners" button removes the winners.
- Winners get the "Winner" mark on the leaderboard, and their phones show "You won!". Both update live.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Quizzy

A live quiz app for conference talks. The moderator prepares quizzes under
`/moderate` and runs games from the big screen; the audience joins on their phones.

## Run it

```sh
RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 \
SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... \
bin/serve
```

`bin/serve` prepares the databases (under `storage/`) and the assets, then runs the
app in the foreground on all interfaces. `GET /up` returns 200 when the app is ready.

Every page under `/moderate` asks for the moderator's HTTP Basic credentials.

To move a quiz to another Quizzy, use its "Export" page (JSON to copy) and the
"Import quiz" button on `/moderate`. The format is described in `docs/quiz-json-format.md`.

## Run a game

On the quiz page, **Start a game** opens the big screen. Show the join link and the
QR code; the audience opens the link on a phone, types a name and taps **Join**.
Then **Start**, **Finish**, **Next** and **End quiz** move the game along. Several
games per quiz are fine (a rehearsal, then the real talk). Open the big screen on
the address the phones can reach, since the join link uses the address in the
browser's address bar.

The rules, the screens and the live updates are described in `docs/live-game.md`.

## Develop and test

```sh
bundle install
bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails test                       # unit and request tests
bin/rails test:system                # all browser tests (Cuprite + headless Chromium)
bin/rails test test/system/layout_test.rb   # one browser test file
bin/rubocop
bin/brakeman
```

For the browser tests, `BROWSER_PATH` points at Chromium (default `/usr/bin/chromium`).

Design notes, mockups and the reasoning behind decisions live in `docs/`.

# Quizzy: design notes

Living notes for the next steps. The design itself lives in `docs/mockups/`
(style guide, quiz page, question form; `quizzy.css` and the Inter font are the
design's assets). This file records what we built and why.

## Scope of this release

The moderator side only:

- quizzes (list, create, settings, delete)
- questions with text options, ordering, activation, delete
- the preview: a player-style run through the active questions
- export and import of a quiz as JSON, to move it to another conference or to a
  colleague's Quizzy (see `quiz-json-format.md`)

The live game (see `live-game.md`): a game per play of a quiz, the big screen with
the lobby, questions, counts and results, the players' phones (join, answer, see
the result), and live updates everywhere without page reloads.

Not built yet: leaderboards and a results page after the game. The design CSS
already has classes for them.

## Running

`bin/serve` is the only entry point. With `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT`,
`SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`
set, it:

1. checks the variables (exits if one is missing),
2. checks the bundle is satisfied from the local gems (`bundle install --local` as
   fallback, never the network),
3. runs `db:prepare` (creates and migrates every production SQLite database),
4. runs `assets:precompile` into `public/assets`,
5. `exec`s `rails server` on `0.0.0.0:$PORT` in the foreground.

Data lives only under `storage/`: `production.sqlite3` (app), plus the Solid
Cache, Queue and Cable databases. Logs go to STDOUT. `GET /up` is the health check.

## Routes

| Path | Screen |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | redirects to `/moderate` |
| `/moderate` | quiz list, "New quiz" |
| `/moderate/quizzes/new` | quiz form (Title, "Save quiz") |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id` | quiz page: questions, "Add question", "Settings", "Preview" |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/edit` | "Settings": same quiz form, "Delete quiz" (confirm) |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/preview` | player-style run of the active questions |
| `/moderate/quizzes/:id/export` | the quiz as JSON in a `<pre>` ("Export" link on the quiz page) |
| `/moderate/import/new` | "Quiz JSON" text area and "Import" ("Import quiz" button on `/moderate`) |
| `POST /moderate/import` | creates a new quiz from the JSON, or re-renders with the errors (422) |
| `POST /moderate/quizzes/:id/games` | "Start a game" on the quiz page (creates a game) |
| `/moderate/games/:id` | the big screen of a game (lobby, questions, results, "The quiz is over") |
| `/moderate/games/:id/live` | the big screen's live fragment (ETag) |
| `POST /moderate/games/:id/start`, `finish`, `next`, `end_quiz` | the game's buttons |
| `/play/:code` | the join link: "Your name" and "Join", then the phone's view (public) |
| `/play/:code/state`, `POST /play/:code/join`, `POST /play/:code/answer` | the phone's live fragment, join, tap |
| `/mo",
  "output_tail": " | -------------------------------------- |
| `lobby`  | title, join link, QR, Players: N  | **Start** (disabled without active questions); **End quiz** only when there are none | join form, or "Waiting for the quiz to start…" |
| `open`   | question N of M, options, Answers | **Finish**                             | question and option buttons            |
| `closed` | question N of M, counts, Correct  | **Next**, or **End quiz** on the last  | result: Correct! / Wrong! / No answer  |
| `ended`  | The quiz is over                  | none                                   | The quiz is over                       |

Moves are compare-and-set: the phase is read again inside the transaction, so a
second click on **Finish** (or two moderators) does nothing, and the moderator is
told "The game has already moved on. Look at the screen."

## Data

- `games`: `quiz_id`, `title` (copied), `code` (5 characters, unique, no 0/O/1/I),
  `phase`, `position` (question on screen; 0 in the lobby), `revision`, `progress`,
  `ended_at`.
- `game_questions`, `game_options`: a **copy** of the quiz's *active* questions and
  options, made when the game is created (`Game.create_from_quiz!`). Editing or
  deleting questions later changes neither a running game nor a played one. Inactive
  questions are not copied, so games skip them and "of M" counts only active ones.
- `players`: `game_id`, `name` (1 to 40 characters, trimmed).
- `answers`: one row per player per question (unique). Picking again updates it.
  An answer is only accepted while its question is open, and only for an option
  of that question.

Deleting a quiz deletes its games, their players and answers.

## Players and the browser

The browser remembers its player in the session cookie: `session[:players]` maps a
game's code to the player's id. Opening the join link again continues as the same
player. Each game has its own entry (up to 20 games per browser), so a browser can
play two games. Another browser is another player.

## Who sees what (the secret)

The correct options are never sent to a phone or to the big screen before their
question is closed:

- the phone's view (`play/_state`) renders no correct flags while the question is open;
- the big screen (`moderate/games/_screen`) renders counts and "Correct" only when closed;
- the state endpoint `GET /play/:code/state` returns the same partial, so it is covered too;
- the broadcasts carry no content, only a tick (see below).

A live quiz app for conference talks. The moderator prepares quizzes under
`/moderate` and runs games from the big screen; the audience joins on their phones.

## Run it

```sh
RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 \
SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... \
bin/serve
```

`bin/serve` prepares the databases (under `storage/`) and the assets, then runs the
app in the foreground on all interfaces. `GET /up` returns 200 when the app is ready.

Every page under `/moderate` asks for the moderator's HTTP Basic credentials.

To move a quiz to another Quizzy, use its "Export" page (JSON to copy) and the
"Import quiz" button on `/moderate`. The format is described in `docs/quiz-json-format.md`.

## Run a game

On the quiz page, **Start a game** opens the big screen. Show the join link and the
QR code; the audience opens the link on a phone, types a name and taps **Join**.
Then **Start**, **Finish**, **Next** and **End quiz** move the game along. Several
games per quiz are fine (a rehearsal, then the real talk). Open the big screen on
the address the phones can reach, since the join link uses the address in the
browser's address bar.

The rules, the screens and the live updates are described in `docs/live-game.md`.

## Develop and test

```sh
bundle install
bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails test                       # unit and request tests
bin/rails test:system                # all browser tests (Cuprite + headless Chromium)
bin/rails test test/system/layout_test.rb   # one browser test file
bin/rubocop
bin/brakeman
```

For the browser tests, `BROWSER_PATH` points at Chromium (default `/usr/bin/chromium`).

Design notes, mockups and the reasoning behind decisions live in `docs/`.

# Live game: design notes

A **game** is one play of a quiz: a rehearsal, the real talk, the next conference.
Each game has its own join link, players and answers. The moderator runs it from a
big-screen page; the audience answers on phones. Nothing here calls an outside
service: everything lives under `storage/`.

## Flow

1. Quiz page: **Start a game** creates the game and opens its big screen
   (`/moderate/games/:id`, moderator login). The games of the quiz are listed below
   the questions, one row each, with a status.
2. **Lobby.** The big screen shows the quiz title, the join link as text
   (`localhost:3000/play/K7RZX`, scheme left out), the same link as a QR code, and
   **Players: N**. Phones open the link, type **Your name**, tap **Join**, and see
   **Hi, Alice!** and "Waiting for the quiz to start…".
3. **Start** opens the first active question: **Question 1 of 3**, the text and the
   options. Phones show the options as buttons. A tap submits at once and marks the
   option **Your answer**; another tap changes it, the last one counts.
   The big screen counts **Answers: 1 / 2** (players who answered / players in the game).
4. **Finish** closes the question. The big screen shows the answers per option
   (**N answers**) and marks the correct options **Correct**. Phones show **Correct!**,
   **Wrong!** or **No answer**, and highlight the right option.
5. **Next** opens the next active question. On the last question the button is
   **End quiz**, which ends the game: the big screen and every phone show
   **The quiz is over**. The join link then shows the same and refuses new players.

Players may join in any phase before the end, including while a question is open.
A player who joins mid-question can answer that question.

## Phases and buttons

| Phase    | Big screen                        | Button(s)                              | Phones                                 |
| -------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `lobby`  | title, join link, QR, Players: N  | **Start** (disabled without active questions); **End quiz** only when there are none | join form, or "Waiting for the quiz to start…" |
| `open`   | question N of M, options, Answers | **Finish**                             | question and option buttons            |
| `closed` | question N of M, counts, Correct  | **Next**, or **End quiz** on the last  | result: Correct! / Wrong! / No answer  |
| `ended`  | The quiz is over                  | none                                   | The quiz is over                       |

Moves are compare-and-set: the phase is read again inside the transaction, so a
second click on **Finish** (or two moderators) does nothing, and the moderator is
told "The game has already moved on. Look at the screen."

## Data

- `games`: `quiz_id`, `title` (copied), `code` (5 characters, unique, no 0/O/1/I),
  `phase`, `position` (question on screen; 0 in the lobby), `revision`, `progress`,
  `ended_at`.
- `game_questions`, `game_options`: a **copy** of the quiz's *active* questions and
  options, made when the game is created (`Game.create_from_quiz!`). Editing or
  deleting questions later changes neither a running game nor a played one. Inactive
  questions are not copied, so games skip them and "of M" counts only active ones.
- `players`: `game_id`, `name` (1 to 40 characters, trimmed).
- `answers`: one row per player per question (unique). Picking again updates it.
  An answer is only accepted while its question is open, and only for an option
  of that question.

Deleting a quiz deletes its games, their players and answers.

## Players and the browser

The browser remembers its player in the session cookie: `session[:players]` maps a
game's code to the player's id. Opening the join link again continues as the same
player. Each game has its own entry (up to 20 games per browser), so a browser can
play two games. Another browser is another player.

## Who sees what (the secret)

The correct options are never sent to a phone or to the big screen before their
question is closed:

- the phone's view (`play/_state`) renders no correct flags while the question is open;
- the big screen (`moderate/games/_screen`) renders counts and "Correct" only when closed;
- the state endpoint `GET /play/:code/state` returns the same partial, so it is covered too;
- the broadcasts carry no content, only a tick (see below).

Tests in `test/integration/play_flow_test.rb` check the HTML and the fragment for
`is-correct`, `data-correct` and "Correct" while a question is open.

## Live updates

The second fetch covers a change sent just before the server registered the new subscription (Action Cable's test adapter registers subscribers asynchronously, and that race showed up in the browser tests). - **No lost typing.** Replacing a region keeps the text a user has typed in its fields and their focus (`live_controller.js`). Lessons, so they are not learned twice: - Turbo's stream identifier is just the stream name. Action Cable keeps one subscription per identifier, and it ignores a second subscribe with the same one. Navigating from one page to the next (which a tap does) then let the old page's unsubscribe remove the new page's subscription, so the phone stopped getting ticks. Each `turbo_stream_from` therefore gets a random `data-subscription` attribute (`live_subscription` helper), which makes every identifier unique. - The poll and the `connected` catch-up are not optional. Without them, a phone on crowded Wi-Fi shows a stale question until the next change. - `fresh_when`/`stale?` renders the 304 itself. Calling `render` after it raises a double-render error. Use `render ... if stale?(...)`. - Propshaft: `public/assets/.manifest.json` (from `bin/serve` or `assets:precompile`) makes the test environment use the static resolver, which does not know new stylesheets until the next precompile. Delete `public/assets` when adding a stylesheet and running the tests by hand. ## Layout notes - The big screen (`layouts/screen.html.erb`) uses the design's `cover`, `screen`, `lobby`, `stage-*` classes. Controls sit in the dark `screen-controls` bar. - Phones (`layouts/play.html.erb`) use the `play-*` classes. - The live region has `display: contents`, so the page layout is unchanged. - Counters are `inline-flex` pills. Their text must sit in one inline element (`Players: 2`), or browsers put "Players:" and "2" on separate lines and the text "Players: 2" is no longer found. - The join link is built from the request host. The moderator should open the big screen on the address the phones use (for example the laptop's LAN address), not `localhost`, or the phones cannot reach the link. ## Routes | Method and path | What | | --- | --- | | `POST /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/games` | "Start a game" | | `GET /moderate/games/:id` | the big screen | | `GET /moderate/games/:id/live` | the big screen's live fragment (ETag) | | `POST /moderate/games/:id/start`, `finish`, `next`, `end_quiz` | the buttons | | `GET /play/:code` | the join link: join form, or the phone's view | | `GET /play/:code/state` | the phone's live fragment (ETag) | | `POST /play/:code/join` | "Join" (`player[name]`) | | `POST /play/:code/answer` | a tap (`game_option_id`) | The player routes are public (no login). Unknown codes show "No such quiz" with 404. ## Labels the QA tests rely on Buttons: "Start a game", "Start", "Finish", "Next", "End quiz", "Join". Fields: "Your name" (label). Texts: "Players: 2", "Join at", the join link, "Question 1 of 3", "Answers: 1 / 2", "Correct", "Correct!", "Wrong!", "No answer", "Your answer", "Hi, Alice!", "The quiz is over", "Waiting for the quiz to start…". No confirmation dialog on "End quiz": the flow the moderator is asked to follow is Finish, Next, End quiz, and the button is plain, so a dialog would be an extra step. ## Tests - `test/models/game_test.rb`: the copy, codes, every transition and its refusals, answers (last pick, only the open question, only own game), joins, broadcasts. - `test/integration/game_moderation_test.rb`: login on every game route, Start a game, each phase of the big screen, the buttons, ETag on the live fragment. - `test/integration/play_flow_test.rb`: join, rejoin, another browser, two games in one browser, late join and the end, answers, the no-leak checks, ETags. - `test/system/live_game_test.rb`: a whole game in four browsers (moderator and three phones), a missed update caught up by the poll, typing kept during an update, two games in one browser. Verified against `bin/serve` in production mode too (solid_cable): a scripted game with a moderator and two phones (live counters and results within a fraction of a second), and a phone taken offline and back (it catches up within a fraction of a second of reconnecting).

messages.content:
{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# One play of a quiz: its own players, answers and questions.
#
# A game copies the quiz's active questions and their options when it is
# created (see .create_from_quiz!), so editing the quiz later changes neither a
# running game nor one that was already played. Inactive questions are skipped.
#
# Phases, in order (the moderator's button is in brackets):
#
#   lobby   players join; nothing is open yet                      [Start]
#   open    question #position accepts answers                    [Finish]
#   closed  question #position is closed; the answers are shown   [Next], or [End quiz] on the last one
#   ended   the quiz is over: nobody joins or answers any more
#
# Players may join in any phase but "ended".
#
# Live updates (see application.js): every change bumps `revision` and ticks the
# big screen, which shows the counts. Only a move (start, finish, next, end)
# bumps `progress` and ticks the phones, so a room of phones does not refetch
# on every answer.
class Game < ApplicationRecord
  PHASES = %w[lobby open closed ended].freeze
  # No 0, O, 1 or I: the code is read aloud and typed on phones.
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5
  # What the server sends to a live page: "something changed, fetch your view".
  TICK = '<turbo-stream action="tick"></turbo-stream>'.freeze

  belongs_to :quiz, inverse_of: :games
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game
  has_many :players, -> { order(:id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game

  normalizes :title, with: ->(title) { title.strip }

  validates :title, presence: true
  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true, format: { with: /\A[A-Z2-9]{#{CODE_LENGTH}}\z/ }
  validates :phase, inclusion: { in: PHASES }
  validates :position, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }

  before_validation :assign_code, on: :create

  # Creates a game from the quiz's active questions, with their options.
  def self.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    transaction do
      game = create!(quiz: quiz, title: quiz.title)
      quiz.questions.active.includes(:options).each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        game_question = game.game_questions.create!(position: position, text: question.text)
        question.options.each.with_index(1) do |option, option_position|
          game_question.options.create!(position: option_position, text: option.text, correct: option.correct)
        end
      end
      game
    end
  end

  # A code that no game uses yet.
  def self.unused_code
    loop do
      code = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.size)] }.join
      return code unless exists?(code: code)
    end
  end

  # Names of the Action Cable streams the live pages subscribe to.
  def live_stream_name = "quizzy_game_#{id}"
  def play_stream_name = "quizzy_game_#{id}_play"

  def lobby? = phase == "lobby"
  def open? = phase == "open"
  def closed? = phase == "closed"
  def ended? = phase == "ended"

  def total_questions
    game_questions.count
  end

  def last_question?
    position == total_questions
  end

  # The question on screen (open or closed), or nil in the lobby.
  def current_question
    game_questions.find_by(position: position) unless lobby? || position.zero?
  end

  def players_count
    players.count
  end

  # How many players have answered the question on screen.
  def answers_count
    current_question ? current_question.answers.count : 0
  end

  # The player's pick for the question on screen, if any.
  def answer_of(player)
    question = current_question
    question && player && player.answer_for(question)
  end

  # Moderator actions. Each returns true when the game moved, and false when it
  # was not in a phase that allows the action (for example, a second click on
  # "Finish"). The state is read again inside the transaction, so two moderators
  # clicking at once cannot move the game twice.

  def start!
    move { [ "open", 1 ] if lobby? && total_questions.positive? }
  end

  def finish!
    move { [ "closed", position ] if open? }
  end

  def next_question!
    move { [ "open", position + 1 ] if closed? && position < total_questions }
  end

  def end_quiz!
    move { [ "ended", position ] if lobby? || closed? }
  end

  # Player actions.

  # Adds a player. Returns the player. It is unsaved, with errors, when the name
  # is not valid or the quiz is over.
  def join(name)
    player = players.new(name: name)
    saved = transaction do
      next false if Game.where(id: id, phase: "ended").exists?

      player.save && bump_revision!
    end
    broadcast_change if saved
    player
  end

  # Records the player's pick for the question on screen. The last pick counts.
  # Returns false when the question is not open, or the option is not on it.
  def answer!(player, option)
    saved = transaction do
      reload
      question = current_question
      next false unless open? && question && option.game_question_id == question.id && player.game_id == id

      Answer.find_or_initialize_by(player: player, game_question: question).update!(game_option: option)
      bump_revision!
    end
    broadcast_change if saved
    saved
  end

  private

  def assign_code
    self.code = self.class.unused_code if code.blank?
  end

  # Runs the block with the freshly read game. The block returns [phase, position]
  # for the move, or nil when the move is not allowed from the current state.
  def move
    moved = transaction do
      reload
      target_phase, target_position = yield
      next false unless target_phase

      now = Time.current
      update_columns(phase: target_phase, position: target_position, progress: progress + 1,
                     revision: revision + 1, updated_at: now)
      game_questions.where(position: target_position).update_all(opened_at: now) if target_phase == "open"
      game_questions.where(position: target_position).update_all(closed_at: now) if target_phase == "closed"
      update_columns(ended_at: now) if target_phase == "ended"
      true
    end
    reload
    broadcast_change(moved: true) if moved
    moved
  end

  def bump_revision!
    increment!(:revision)
    true
  end

  def broadcast_change(moved: false)
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to(live_stream_name, content: TICK)
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to(play_stream_name, content: TICK) if moved
  end
end
"
}

# A single-choice question with text options.
#
# Options are edited as "rows" (see #option_rows=). Rows with blank text are
# skipped. A question needs at least two options and at least one of them must
# be correct. Rules are checked before anything is written; the options are
# replaced in the same transaction as the question.
class Question < ApplicationRecord
  MIN_OPTIONS = 2
  FORM_OPTION_ROWS = 4

  belongs_to :quiz, inverse_of: :questions
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :question

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }

  normalizes :text, with: ->(text) { text.strip }

  validates :text, presence: true
  validate :validate_option_rows, if: -> { @option_rows }

  before_create :place_at_end
  after_save :save_option_rows, if: -> { @option_rows }

  # Rows as typed in the form: [{ text:, correct: }, ...], in display order.
  # Assigning rows does not touch the database until the question is saved.
  attr_reader :option_rows

  def option_rows=(rows)
    @option_rows = Array(rows).map do |row|
      { text: row[:text].to_s, correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) == true }
    end
  end

  # Rows to show in the form: what was typed, or the saved options, padded to
  # FORM_OPTION_ROWS so the form always has room for new options.
  def form_option_rows
    rows = @option_rows || options.map { |option| { text: option.text, correct: option.correct } }
    rows + Array.new([ FORM_OPTION_ROWS - rows.size, 0 ].max) { { text: "", correct: false } }
  end

  def move_up
    move_by(-1)
  end

  def move_down
    move_by(1)
  end

  private

  def kept_option_rows
    (@option_rows || []).select { |row| row[:text].strip.present? }
  end

  def validate_option_rows
    kept = kept_option_rows
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if kept.size < MIN_OPTIONS
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if kept.none? { |row| row[:correct] }
  end

  def save_option_rows
    Option.where(question_id: id).delete_all
    kept_option_rows.each.with_index(1) do |row, position|
      Option.create!(question: self, text: row[:text].strip, correct: row[:correct], position: position)
    end
    @option_rows = nil
    options.reset
  end

  def place_at_end
    self.position = quiz.questions.maximum(:position).to_i + 1
  end

  def move_by(step)
    ordered = quiz.questions.reorder(:position, :id).to_a
    index = ordered.index { |question| question.id == id }
    target = index && index + step
    return if index.nil? || target.negative? || target >= ordered.size

    ordered[index], ordered[target] = ordered[target], ordered[index]
    Question.transaction do
      ordered.each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        question.update_column(:position, position) unless question.position == position
      end
    end
    reload
  end
end

    rows + Array.new([ FORM_OPTION_ROWS - rows.size, 0 ].max) { { text: "", correct: false } }
  end

  def move_up
    move_by(-1)
  end

  def move_down
    move_by(1)
  end

  private

  def kept_option_rows
    (@option_rows || []).select { |row| row[:text].strip.present? }
  end

  def validate_option_rows
    kept = kept_option_rows
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if kept.size < MIN_OPTIONS
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if kept.none? { |row| row[:correct] }
  end

  def save_option_rows
    Option.where(question_id: id).delete_all
    kept_option_rows.each.with_index(1) do |row, position|
      Option.create!(question: self, text: row[:text].strip, correct: row[:correct], position: position)
    end
    @option_rows = nil
    options.reset
  end

  def place_at_end
    self.position = quiz.questions.maximum(:position).to_i + 1
  end

  def move_by(step)
    ordered = quiz.questions.reorder(:position, :id).to_a
    index = ordered.index { |question| question.id == id }
    target = index && index + step
    return if index.nil? || target.negative? || target >= ordered.size

    ordered[index], ordered[target] = ordered[target], ordered[index]
    Question.transaction do
      ordered.each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        question.update_column(:position, position) unless question.position == position
      end
    end
    reload
  end

# The players' side: the join link and the phone pages. It is public (no
# moderator login). The browser remembers each player in the session, keyed by
# the game's code, so opening the join link again continues as the same player.
class PlayController < ApplicationController
  MAX_REMEMBERED_GAMES = 20

  layout "play"

  helper_method :current_player

  before_action :set_game

  rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound do
    render "missing", status: :not_found
  end

  def show
  end

  # The part of the phone page that changes. The page fetches it on every tick.
  # The ETag changes with the moves of the game and with this player's own pick, so
  # an unchanged view is answered with 304 and a changed one is never served stale.
  def state
    answer = @game.answer_of(current_player)
    return unless stale?(etag: [ @game.progress, current_player&.id, answer&.game_option_id ])

    render partial: "play/state", locals: { game: @game, player: current_player, name: "" }
  end

  def join
    # A second submit (a double tap) or a browser that already joined changes nothing.
    return redirect_to(play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other) if @game.ended? || current_player

    player = @game.join(player_params[:name].to_s)
    if player.persisted?
      remember(player)
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    else
      @typed_name = player_params[:name].to_s
      @join_errors = player.errors.full_messages
      render :show, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  def answer
    option = GameOption.find_by(id: params[:game_option_id])
    if current_player && option && @game.answer!(current_player, option)
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    else
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), alert: refusal(option), status: :see_other
    end
  end

  private

  def set_game
    @game = Game.find_by!(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
  end

  def current_player
    return @current_player if defined?(@current_player)

    id = session[:players]&.[](@game.code)
    @current_player = id && @game.players.find_by(id: id)
  end

  def remember(player)
    players = (session[:players] || {}).to_h.merge(@game.code => player.id)
    session[:players] = players.to_a.last(MAX_REMEMBERED_GAMES).to_h
  end

  def player_params
    params.fetch(:player, {}).permit(:name)
  end

  def refusal(option)
    if @game.ended?
      "The quiz is over."
    elsif current_player.nil?
      "Join the quiz first."
    elsif !@game.open? || option.nil?
      "This question is closed."
    else
      "That answer was not accepted."
    end
  end
end

  # Everything under /moderate needs the moderator's HTTP Basic credentials.

    prepend_before_action :require_moderator

    def require_moderator
      authenticate_or_request_with_http_basic("Quizzy moderator") do |username, password|
        moderator_credentials?(username, password)
      end
    end

    def moderator_credentials?(username, password)
      expected_username = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"].to_s
      expected_password = ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"].to_s
      return false if expected_username.empty? || expected_password.empty?

      ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(username.to_s, expected_username) &&
        ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(password.to_s, expected_password)
    end
  end

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Async adapter only works within the same process, so for manually triggering cable updates from a console,
# and seeing results in the browser, you must do so from the web console (running inside the dev process),
# not a terminal started via bin/rails console! Add "console" to any action or any ERB template view
# to make the web console appear.
development:
  adapter: async

test:
  adapter: test

production:
  adapter: solid_cable
  connects_to:
    database:
      writing: cable
  polling_interval: 0.1.seconds
  message_retention: 1.day
  writer_batch_size: 4
  writer_batch_delay: 0.001.seconds
====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Quizzy: prepare the app and run it in production mode, in the foreground.
#
#   RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
#   QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... bin/serve
#
# Everything the app needs lives under storage/ (SQLite databases) and
# public/assets (precompiled files). Nothing here talks to external services.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export RAILS_ENV="${RAILS_ENV:-production}"
export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"

for name in SECRET_KEY_BASE QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD; do
  if [ -z "${!name:-}" ]; then
    echo "bin/serve: $name must be set" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

# Gems come from the local installation; resolving them must not need the network.
bundle check >/dev/null 2>&1 || bundle install --local

mkdir -p storage tmp/pids log

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Quizzy: prepare the app and run it in production mode, in the foreground.
#
#   RAILS_ENV=production PORT=3000 SECRET_KEY_BASE=... \
#   QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME=... QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD=... bin/serve
#
# Everything the app needs lives under storage/ (SQLite databases) and
# public/assets (precompiled files). Nothing here talks to external services.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export RAILS_ENV="${RAILS_ENV:-production}"
export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"

for name in SECRET_KEY_BASE QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD; do
  if [ -z "${!name:-}" ]; then
    echo "bin/serve: $name must be set" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

# Gems come from the local installation; resolving them must not need the network.
bundle check >/dev/null 2>&1 || bundle install --local

mkdir -p storage tmp/pids log
rm -f tmp/pids/server.pid

bin/rails db:prepare
bin/rails assets:precompile

exec bin/rails server --environment "$RAILS_ENV" --binding 0.0.0.0 --port "$PORT" --pid tmp/pids/server.pid

# A whole game in real browsers: the moderator's big screen and three phones,
# each in its own browser session (so each has its own cookies).
class LiveGameTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include GameFixtures

  setup do
    @quiz = build_quiz_with_questions
  end

  test "a game runs from the join link to the end, and every screen follows it live" do
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    click_button "Start a game"

    assert_text "Players: 0"
    code = find(".lobby__url").text[%r{/play/(\w+)\z}, 1]
    assert_match(/\A[A-Z2-9]{5}\z/, code)
    assert_text "Frontend Fest 2026"
    assert_selector ".qr svg"

    using_session(:alice) { join_as("Alice") }
    assert_text "Players: 1"

    using_session(:bob) { join_as("Bob") }
    using_session(:carol) { join_as("Carol") }
    assert_text "Players: 3"

    click_button "Start"
    assert_text "Question 1 of 3"
    assert_text "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?"
    assert_text "Answers: 0 / 3"
    using_session(:alice) { assert_text "Which HTTP status code means" }

    using_session(:alice) { click_button "429" }
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 3"
    using_session(:alice) { assert_selector ".play-option.is-picked", text: "429" }

    using_session(:bob) { click_button "418" }
    assert_text "Answers: 2 / 3"

    # Changing the answer keeps the count and moves the pick.
    using_session(:bob) { click_button "503" }
    assert_text "Answers: 2 / 3"
    using_session(:bob) do
      assert_selector ".play-option.is-picked", text: "503"
      assert_no_selector ".play-option.is-picked", text: "418"
    end

    click_button "Finish"
    assert_text "Answers: 2 / 3"
    assert_selector ".stage-option.is-correct", text: "429"
    assert_selector ".stage-option__mark", text: "Correct"
    using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Correct!"
      assert_selector ".play-option.is-correct", text: "429"
    end
    using_session(:bob) { assert_text "Wrong!" }
    using_session(:carol) { assert_text "No answer" }

    click_button "Next"
    assert_text "Question 2 of 3"
    using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Which protocol keeps a two-way connection?"
      assert_no_text "Correct!"
    end

    click_button "Finish"
    click_button "Next"
    assert_text "Question 3 of 3"
    click_button "Finish"
    assert_button "End quiz"
    assert_no_button "Next"

    click_button "End quiz"
    assert_text "The quiz is over"
    using_session(:alice) { assert_text "The quiz is over" }
    using_session(:bob) { assert_text "The quiz is over" }
  end

  test "the screens catch up after a missed update, without a reload" do
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    click_button "Start a game"
    game = Game.last
    using_session(:alice) { join_as("Alice") }
    assert_text "Players: 1"

    # A change that nobody is told about (as when Wi-Fi drops for a moment).
    game.increment!(:revision, touch: false)
    Player.create!(game: game, name: "Quiet")
    assert_text "Players: 2", wait: 12
  end

  test "text a player is typing survives an update from the game" do
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    click_button "Start a game"
    game = Game.last

    using_session(:alice) do
      visit "/play/#{game.code}"
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Ali"
      # Someone else joins while Alice types: her page is updated under her.
      game.join("Bob")
      assert_field "Your name", with: "Ali", wait: 8
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
    end
    assert_text "Players: 2"
  end

  test "the join link works for a second game in the same browser, and players are counted per game" do
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    click_button "Start a game"
    first_code = Game.last.code
    using_session(:alice) { join_as("Alice") }

    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{@quiz.id}"
    click_button "Start a game"
    assert_text "Players: 0"

    using_session(:alice) do
      visit "/play/#{first_code}"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
      visit "/play/#{Game.last.code}"
      assert_selector "label", text: "Your name"
    end
  end

  private

  def join_as(name)
    visit "/play/#{Game.last.code}"
    fill_in "Your name", with: name
    click_button "Join"
    assert_text "Hi, #{name}!"
  end
end

cd /app && cat > app/models/leaderboard.rb <<'EOF'
# How a finished game is ranked, and who wins prizes. Plain Ruby: nothing here
# reads or writes the database, so the rules can be tested on their own. Game
# stores the result (see Game#rank_players!) and the winners.
#
# Ranking (see .rank): more points first. Equal points: the lower total time of
# the correct answers wins. An answer's time runs from the moment its question
# opened to the player's last pick. Still equal: whoever joined first.
#
# Winners: a player with 0 points never wins. If fewer than N players have points,
# all of them win. .top takes the first N places. .draw takes everyone with more
# points than the N-th place, and fills the rest at random among the players with
# exactly the N-th place's points (speed does not count there).
class Leaderboard
  Standing = Struct.new(:player, :points, :speed_micros, :place, keyword_init: true)

  # One Standing per player, in place order (place 1 first).
  def self.rank(players)
    standings = players.map do |player|
      correct = player.answers.select { |answer| answer.game_option.correct? }
      Standing.new(player: player, points: correct.size, speed_micros: correct.sum { |answer| answer_micros(answer) })
    end
    ranked = standings.sort_by { |standing| [ -standing.points, standing.speed_micros, standing.player.id ] }
    ranked.each_with_index { |standing, index| standing.place = index + 1 }
    ranked
  end

  # The time of one answer, in whole microseconds (integers compare exactly).
  def self.answer_micros(answer)
    opened = answer.game_question.opened_at
    picked = answer.picked_at || answer.updated_at
    return 0 unless opened && picked

    [ ((picked - opened) * 1_000_000).round, 0 ].max
  end

  # The players with at least one point, in the order they are given (place order).
  def self.scorers(ranked)
    ranked.select { |entry| entry.points.positive? }
  end

  # "Top N": the first N places that have points. `ranked` responds to #points and
  # is in place order (Game passes players; tests can pass anything similar).
  def self.top(ranked, count)
    return [] unless count.positive?

    scorers(ranked).first(count)
  end

  # "Draw": the winners of a tie. Everyone with more points than the N-th place
  # wins. The remaining prizes go at random to the players with exactly the N-th
  # place's points. Each call draws again.
  def self.draw(ranked, count, random: Random.new)
    return [] unless count.positive?

    scored = scorers(ranked)
    return scored if scored.size <= count

    cutoff = scored[count - 1].points
    ahead = scored.select { |entry| entry.points > cutoff }
    tied = scored.select { |entry| entry.points == cutoff }
    ahead + tied.sample(count - ahead.size, random: random)
  end
end
EOF

cd /app && cat > app/models/game.rb <<'EOF'
# One play of a quiz: its own players, answers and questions.
#
# A game copies the quiz's active questions and their options when it is
# created (see .create_from_quiz!), so editing the quiz later changes neither a
# running game nor one that was already played. Inactive questions are skipped.
#
# Phases, in order (the moderator's button is in brackets):
#
#   lobby   players join; nothing is open yet                      [Start]
#   open    question #position accepts answers                    [Finish]
#   closed  question #position is closed; the answers are shown   [Next], or [End quiz] on the last one
#   ended   the quiz is over: nobody joins or answers any more    (the leaderboard, then the winners)
#
# Players may join in any phase but "ended".
#
# Ending ranks the players and stores each one's result (points, speed, place) on
# the player (see Leaderboard). After the end the moderator picks the winners
# (Top N, Draw, Reset winners). The winners can change any number of times.
#
# Live updates (see application.js): every change bumps `revision` and ticks the
# big screen, which shows the counts. A move (start, finish, next, end) and a
# change of winners bump `progress` and tick the phones too, so a room of phones
# does not refetch on every answer.
class Game < ApplicationRecord
  PHASES = %w[lobby open closed ended].freeze
  # No 0, O, 1 or I: the code is read aloud and typed on phones.
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5
  # What the server sends to a live page: "something changed, fetch your view".
  TICK = '<turbo-stream action="tick"></turbo-stream>'.freeze

  belongs_to :quiz, inverse_of: :games
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game
  has_many :players, -> { order(:id) }, dependent: :destroy, inverse_of: :game

  normalizes :title, with: ->(title) { title.strip }

  validates :title, presence: true
  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true, format: { with: /\A[A-Z2-9]{#{CODE_LENGTH}}\z/ }
  validates :phase, inclusion: { in: PHASES }
  validates :position, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }

  before_validation :assign_code, on: :create

  # Creates a game from the quiz's active questions, with their options.
  def self.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
    transaction do
      game = create!(quiz: quiz, title: quiz.title)
      quiz.questions.active.includes(:options).each.with_index(1) do |question, position|
        game_question = game.game_questions.create!(position: position, text: question.text)
        question.options.each.with_index(1) do |option, option_position|
          game_question.options.create!(position: option_position, text: option.text, correct: option.correct)
        end
      end
      game
    end
  end

  # A code that no game uses yet.
  def self.unused_code
    loop do
      code = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.size)] }.join
      return code unless exists?(code: code)
    end
  end

  # Names of the Action Cable streams the live pages subscribe to.
  def live_stream_name = "quizzy_game_#{id}"
  def play_stream_name = "quizzy_game_#{id}_play"

  def lobby? = phase == "lobby"
  def open? = phase == "open"
  def closed? = phase == "closed"
  def ended? = phase == "ended"

  def total_questions
    game_questions.count
  end

  def last_question?
    position == total_questions
  end

  # The question on screen (open or closed), or nil in the lobby.
  def current_question
    game_questions.find_by(position: position) unless lobby? || position.zero?
  end

  def players_count
    players.count
  end

  # How many players have answered the question on screen.
  def answers_count
    current_question ? current_question.answers.count : 0
  end

  # The player's pick for the question on screen, if any.
  def answer_of(player)
    question = current_question
    question && player && player.answer_for(question)
  end

  # The players in place order. Only meaningful after the end, when the places
  # are stored.
  def ranked_players
    players.reorder(:place, :id).to_a
  end

  # How many winners the moderator asked for. It is read from the quiz as it is
  # now, so a change in the settings applies until the winners are picked.
  def winners_count
    Quiz.where(id: quiz_id).pick(:winners_count)
  end

  # Moderator actions. Each returns true when the game moved, and false when it
  # was not in a phase that allows the action (for example, a second click on
  # "Finish"). The state is read again inside the transaction, so two moderators
  # clicking at once cannot move the game twice.

  def start!
    move { [ "open", 1 ] if lobby? && total_questions.positive? }
  end

  def finish!
    move { [ "closed", position ] if open? }
  end

  def next_question!
    move { [ "open", position + 1 ] if closed? && position < total_questions }
  end

  def end_quiz!
    move { [ "ended", position ] if lobby? || closed? }
  end

  # Winner actions, after the end only. Each returns the new winners (an array,
  # possibly empty), or nil when the game is not over. The winners are chosen and
  # stored in one transaction, so the screens and phones get the same answer.

  def pick_top_winners!
    choose_winners { |ranked| Leaderboard.top(ranked, winners_count) }
  end

  def draw_winners!
    choose_winners { |ranked| Leaderboard.draw(ranked, winners_count) }
  end

  def reset_winners!
    choose_winners { [] }
  end

  # Player actions.

  # Adds a player. Returns the player. It is unsaved, with errors, when the name
  # is not valid or the quiz is over.
  def join(name)
    player = players.new(name: name)
    saved = transaction do
      next false if Game.where(id: id, phase: "ended").exists?

      player.save && bump_revision!
    end
    broadcast_change if saved
    player
  end

  # Records the player's pick for the question on screen. The last pick counts,
  # and its time is kept (picked_at) for the speed ranking. Returns false when the
  # question is not open, or the option is not on it.
  def answer!(player, option)
    saved = transaction do
      reload
      question = current_question
      next false unless open? && question && option.game_question_id == question.id && player.game_id == id

      Answer.find_or_initialize_by(player: player, game_question: question)
            .update!(game_option: option, picked_at: Time.current)
      bump_revision!
    end
    broadcast_change if saved
    saved
  end

  private

  def assign_code
    self.code = self.class.unused_code if code.blank?
  end

  # Runs the block with the freshly read game. The block returns [phase, position]
  # for the move, or nil when the move is not allowed from the current state.
  def move
    moved = transaction do
      reload
      target_phase, target_position = yield
      next false unless target_phase

      now = Time.current
      update_columns(phase: target_phase, position: target_position, progress: progress + 1,
                     revision: revision + 1, updated_at: now)
      game_questions.where(position: target_position).update_all(opened_at: now) if target_phase == "open"
      game_questions.where(position: target_position).update_all(closed_at: now) if target_phase == "closed"
      if target_phase == "ended"
        update_columns(ended_at: now)
        rank_players!
      end
      true
    end
    reload
    broadcast_change(moved: true) if moved
    moved
  end

  # Stores each player's result. Answers cannot change after the end (answer!
  # refuses them), so the stored result stays right.
  def rank_players!
    Leaderboard.rank(players.includes(answers: %i[game_option game_question]).to_a).each do |standing|
      standing.player.update_columns(points: standing.points, speed_micros: standing.speed_micros,
                                     place: standing.place)
    end
  end

  def choose_winners
    chosen = transaction do
      reload
      next nil unless ended?

      winners = yield(ranked_players)
      Player.where(game_id: id).update_all(winner: false)
      Player.where(id: winners.map(&:id)).update_all(winner: true) if winners.any?
      update_columns(progress: progress + 1, revision: revision + 1, updated_at: Time.current)
      winners
    end
    broadcast_change(moved: true) if chosen
    chosen
  end

  def bump_revision!
    increment!(:revision)
    true
  end

  def broadcast_change(moved: false)
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to(live_stream_name, content: TICK)
    Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_stream_to(play_stream_name, content: TICK) if moved
  end
end
EOF

module Moderate
  # The moderator's side of a live game: starting one from a quiz, the big-screen
  # page, the buttons that move the game on (Start, Finish, Next, End quiz), and
  # the prizes after the end (Top N, Draw, Reset winners).
  class GamesController < BaseController
    before_action :set_game, except: :create

    MOVED_ON = "The game has already moved on. Look at the screen.".freeze
    NOT_OVER = "The winners are picked after the quiz is over.".freeze
    NOBODY_WINS = "No player has points, so nobody wins.".freeze

    # "Start a game" on the quiz page.
    def create
      game = Game.create_from_quiz!(Quiz.find(params[:quiz_id]))
      redirect_to moderate_game_path(game), status: :see_other
    end

    # The big screen.
    def show
      render layout: "screen"
    end

    # The part of the big screen that changes. The page fetches it on every tick.
    # The winners count is part of the ETag: it can change in the quiz settings.
    def live
      render partial: "moderate/games/screen", locals: { game: @game } if stale?(etag: [ @game.revision, @game.winners_count ])
    end

    def start
      if @game.start!
        back_to_screen
      elsif @game.lobby?
        back_to_screen(alert: "This quiz has no active questions to play.")
      else
        back_to_screen(alert: MOVED_ON)
      end
    end

    def finish
      back_to_screen(alert: @game.finish! ? nil : MOVED_ON)
    end

    def next_question
      back_to_screen(alert: @game.next_question! ? nil : MOVED_ON)
    end

    def end_quiz
      back_to_screen(alert: @game.end_quiz! ? nil : MOVED_ON)
    end

    def top_winners
      winners_picked(@game.pick_top_winners!)
    end

    def draw_winners
      winners_picked(@game.draw_winners!)
    end

    def reset_winners
      back_to_screen(alert: @game.reset_winners!.nil? ? NOT_OVER : nil)
    end

    private

    def set_game
      @game = Game.find(params[:id])
    end

    def winners_picked(winners)
      alert = if winners.nil? then NOT_OVER
              elsif winners.empty? then NOBODY_WINS
              end
      back_to_screen(alert: alert)
    end

    def back_to_screen(alert: nil)
      redirect_to moderate_game_path(@game), alert: alert, status: :see_other
    end
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

# The ranking and the winner rules, without the database.
class LeaderboardTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  Option = Struct.new(:correct, keyword_init: true) do
    def correct? = correct
  end
  Question = Struct.new(:opened_at, keyword_init: true)
  Pick = Struct.new(:game_option, :game_question, :picked_at, :updated_at, keyword_init: true)
  Player = Struct.new(:id, :answers, keyword_init: true)
  Entry = Struct.new(:id, :points, :place, keyword_init: true)

  OPENED = Time.utc(2026, 11, 25, 10, 0, 0)

  # One answer: correct or not, picked `seconds` after the question opened.
  def pick(correct:, seconds:, opened: OPENED)
    question = Question.new(opened_at: opened)
    Pick.new(game_option: Option.new(correct: correct), game_question: question,
             picked_at: opened + seconds, updated_at: opened + seconds)
  end

  def player(id, *picks)
    Player.new(id: id, answers: picks)
  end

  def ranked_ids(players)
    Leaderboard.rank(players).map { |standing| standing.player.id }
  end

  test "more points rank higher" do
    standings = Leaderboard.rank([
      player(1, pick(correct: true, seconds: 1)),
      player(2, pick(correct: true, seconds: 1), pick(correct: true, seconds: 2)),
      player(3)
    ])
    assert_equal [ 2, 1, 3 ], standings.map { |s| s.player.id }
    assert_equal [ 2, 1, 0 ], standings.map(&:points)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3 ], standings.map(&:place)
  end

  test "equal points are ranked by the total time of the correct answers" do
    slow = player(1, pick(correct: true, seconds: 5))
    fast = player(2, pick(correct: true, seconds: 2))
    assert_equal [ 2, 1 ], ranked_ids([ slow, fast ])
    standings = Leaderboard.rank([ slow, fast ])
    assert_equal 2_000_000, standings.first.speed_micros
    assert_equal 5_000_000, standings.last.speed_micros
  end

  test "only correct answers count towards the speed" do
    # 1 correct answer at 4 s; a wrong answer at 1 s must not make her faster.
    wrong_fast = player(1, pick(correct: true, seconds: 4), pick(correct: false, seconds: 1, opened: OPENED + 10))
    right_later = player(2, pick(correct: true, seconds: 3))
    assert_equal [ 2, 1 ], ranked_ids([ wrong_fast, right_later ])
  end

  test "the time of an answer runs to the last pick, which is stored in picked_at" do
    question = Question.new(opened_at: OPENED)
    option = Option.new(correct: true)
    # Picked at 1 s, then again at 6 s with the same option: updated_at did not move.
    last_pick = Pick.new(game_option: option, game_question: question,
                         picked_at: OPENED + 6, updated_at: OPENED + 1)
    other = player(2, pick(correct: true, seconds: 3))
    assert_equal [ 2, 1 ], ranked_ids([ player(1, last_pick), other ])
    assert_equal 6_000_000, Leaderboard.rank([ player(1, last_pick) ]).first.speed_micros
  end

  test "the answer time is in whole microseconds" do
    answer = pick(correct: true, seconds: 1.5)
    assert_equal 1_500_000, Leaderboard.answer_micros(answer)
  end

  test "still tied, the player who joined first ranks first" do
    a = player(7, pick(correct: true, seconds: 2))
    b = player(3, pick(correct: true, seconds: 2))
    assert_equal [ 3, 7 ], ranked_ids([ a, b ])
  end

  test "players without points come last, in order of joining" do
    ranked = Leaderboard.rank([ player(5), player(2), player(9, pick(correct: false, seconds: 1)) ])
    assert_equal [ 2, 5, 9 ], ranked.map { |s| s.player.id }
    assert_equal [ 0, 0, 0 ], ranked.map(&:points)
  end

  test "top N is the first N places" do
    ranked = [ Entry.new(id: 1, points: 5, place: 1), Entry.new(id: 2, points: 4, place: 2),
               Entry.new(id: 3, points: 1, place: 3) ]
    assert_equal [ 1, 2 ], Leaderboard.top(ranked, 2).map(&:id)
  end

  test "top N never gives a prize to a player without points" do
    ranked = [ Entry.new(id: 1, points: 2, place: 1), Entry.new(id: 2, points: 0, place: 2),
               Entry.new(id: 3, points: 0, place: 3) ]
    assert_equal [ 1 ], Leaderboard.top(ranked, 3).map(&:id)
    assert_equal [], Leaderboard.top([ Entry.new(id: 1, points: 0, place: 1) ], 3)
  end

  test "a draw gives every player above the N-th place a prize, and the rest at random among the tied" do
    ranked = [ Entry.new(id: 1, points: 5, place: 1), Entry.new(id: 2, points: 4, place: 2),
               Entry.new(id: 3, points: 3, place: 3), Entry.new(id: 4, points: 3, place: 4),
               Entry.new(id: 5, points: 3, place: 5), Entry.new(id: 6, points: 2, place: 6) ]
    seen = Set.new
    200.times do |seed|
      winners = Leaderboard.draw(ranked, 3, random: Random.new(seed)).map(&:id)
      assert_equal 3, winners.size
      assert_includes winners, 1
      assert_includes winners, 2
      seen << (winners - [ 1, 2 ]).first
    end
    assert_equal Set[ 3, 4, 5 ], seen, "every tied player can be drawn, and only they"
  end

    # Same points: place order is speed order, but the draw does not use it.
    ranked = [ Entry.new(id: 1, points: 3, place: 1), Entry.new(id: 2, points: 3, place: 2),
               Entry.new(id: 3, points: 3, place: 3) ]
    winners = (0..200).map { |seed| Leaderboard.draw(ranked, 1, random: Random.new(seed)).first.id }
    assert_equal Set[ 1, 2, 3 ], winners.to_set
  end

  test "the N-th place decides the tie by its points, not by its position among ties" do
    ranked = [ Entry.new(id: 1, points: 4, place: 1), Entry.new(id: 2, points: 3, place: 2),
               Entry.new(id: 3, points: 3, place: 3), Entry.new(id: 4, points: 2, place: 4) ]
    100.times do |seed|
      winners = Leaderboard.draw(ranked, 2, random: Random.new(seed)).map(&:id)
      assert_includes winners, 1
      assert_equal 2, winners.size
      assert_includes [ 2, 3 ], (winners - [ 1 ]).first
    end
  end

  test "a draw with no tie gives exactly the top N" do
    ranked = [ Entry.new(id: 1, points: 5, place: 1), Entry.new(id: 2, points: 4, place: 2),
               Entry.new(id: 3, points: 1, place: 3) ]
    assert_equal [ 1, 2 ], Leaderboard.draw(ranked, 2, random: Random.new(1)).map(&:id)
  end

  test "fewer players with points than N: all of them win, and nobody else" do
    ranked = [ Entry.new(id: 1, points: 2, place: 1), Entry.new(id: 2, points: 1, place: 2),
               Entry.new(id: 3, points: 0, place: 3) ]
    assert_equal [ 1, 2 ], Leaderboard.draw(ranked, 3, random: Random.new(1)).map(&:id)
    assert_equal [ 1, 2 ], Leaderboard.top(ranked, 3).map(&:id)
  end

  test "nobody has points: nobody wins a draw" do
    ranked = [ Entry.new(id: 1, points: 0, place: 1), Entry.new(id: 2, points: 0, place: 2) ]
    assert_equal [], Leaderboard.draw(ranked, 1, random: Random.new(1))
    assert_equal [], Leaderboard.top(ranked, 1)
  end

  test "the draw draws again on each call" do
    ranked = [ Entry.new(id: 1, points: 1, place: 1), Entry.new(id: 2, points: 1, place: 2),
               Entry.new(id: 3, points: 1, place: 3), Entry.new(id: 4, points: 1, place: 4) ]
    results = (0..40).map { Leaderboard.draw(ranked, 1).first.id }
    assert_operator results.uniq.size, :>, 1
  end

require "test_helper"

# Results and prizes of a game, against the database. Time is travelled, so the
# speed of each answer is exact.
class GamePrizesTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActionCable::TestHelper

  BASE = Time.zone.local(2026, 11, 25, 10, 0, 0)

  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Prizes", winners_count: 2)
    add_question("First question")
    add_question("Second question")
    @game = Game.create_from_quiz!(@quiz)
    # Bob joins first, so join order cannot explain a tie that speed should decide.
    travel_to BASE - 60
    @bob = @game.join("Bob")
    @alice = @game.join("Alice")
    @carol = @game.join("Carol")
  end

  # Alice and Bob both answer both questions correctly: Alice in 3 s in total,
  # Bob in 7 s. Carol answers wrongly and has no points.
  def play_out
    travel_to BASE
    @game.start!
    travel_to BASE + 1
    @game.answer!(@carol, option(1, "No"))
    travel_to BASE + 2
    @game.answer!(@alice, option(1, "Yes"))
    travel_to BASE + 5
    @game.answer!(@bob, option(1, "Yes"))
    travel_to BASE + 6
    @game.finish!
    travel_to BASE + 10
    @game.next_question!
    travel_to BASE + 11
    @game.answer!(@alice, option(2, "Yes"))
    travel_to BASE + 12
    @game.answer!(@bob, option(2, "Yes"))
    travel_to BASE + 13
    @game.answer!(@carol, option(2, "No"))
    travel_to BASE + 15
    @game.finish!
    travel_to BASE + 16
    @game.end_quiz!
    @game.reload
  end

  def add_question(text)
    question = @quiz.questions.new(text: text)
    question.option_rows = [ { text: "Yes", correct: true }, { text: "No", correct: false } ]
    question.save!
  end

  def option(position, text)
    @game.game_questions.find_by!(position: position).options.find_by!(text: text)
  end

  def winner_names
    @game.players.where(winner: true).order(:id).map(&:name)
  end

  test "the answer records the time of its last pick, also when the option stays the same" do
    travel_to BASE
    @game.start!
    travel_to BASE + 2
    @game.answer!(@alice, option(1, "Yes"))
    travel_to BASE + 7
    @game.answer!(@alice, option(1, "Yes"))
    assert_equal BASE + 7, @alice.answers.sole.picked_at
  end

  test "the speed counts to the last pick: a changed answer is timed by its last pick" do
    travel_to BASE
    @game.start!
    travel_to BASE + 1
    @game.answer!(@alice, option(1, "Yes"))
    travel_to BASE + 4
    @game.answer!(@alice, option(1, "No"))
    travel_to BASE + 6
    @game.answer!(@alice, option(1, "Yes"))
    travel_to BASE + 8
    @game.finish!
    travel_to BASE + 9
    @game.end_quiz!
    alice = @game.players.find(@alice.id)
    assert_equal 1, alice.points
    assert_equal 6_000_000, alice.speed_micros
  end

  test "ending the quiz stores each player's points, speed and place" do
    play_out

    assert @game.ended?
    alice, bob, carol = @game.players.reload.order(:id).to_a.then { |all| [ @alice, @bob, @carol ].map { |p| all.find { |x| x.id == p.id } } }
    assert_equal [ 2, 2, 0 ], [ alice.points, bob.points, carol.points ]
    assert_equal [ 3_000_000, 7_000_000, 0 ], [ alice.speed_micros, bob.speed_micros, carol.speed_micros ]
    assert_equal [ 1, 2, 3 ], [ alice.place, bob.place, carol.place ]
    assert_equal [ @alice.id, @bob.id, @carol.id ], @game.ranked_players.map(&:id)
  end

  test "joining first does not win a tie: the faster player ranks higher" do
    play_out
    assert_equal %w[Alice Bob Carol], @game.ranked_players.map(&:name)
  end

  test "answers are refused after the end, so the stored result stays" do
    play_out
    assert_not @game.answer!(@carol, option(2, "Yes"))
    assert_equal 0, @carol.answers.count { |answer| answer.game_option.correct? }
    assert_equal 0, @game.players.find(@carol.id).points
  end

  test "Top N makes the first N places the winners" do
    play_out
    winners = @game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_equal %w[Alice Bob], winners.map(&:name)
    assert_equal %w[Alice Bob], winner_names
  end

  test "Top N never gives a prize to a player without points" do
    play_out
    @quiz.update!(winners_count: 3)
    assert_equal %w[Alice Bob], @game.pick_top_winners!.map(&:name)
    assert_not @game.players.find(@carol.id).winner?
  end

  test "Draw gives a tied place to one of the tied players, and draws again on each click" do
    play_out
    @quiz.update!(winners_count: 1)
    seen = Set.new
    30.times do
      winners = @game.draw_winners!
      assert_equal 1, winners.size
      seen << winners.first.name
      assert_equal 1, winner_names.size
    end
    assert_equal Set%w[Alice Bob], seen
  end

  test "Draw with more prizes than tied players gives all the scorers their prize" do
    play_out
    assert_equal %w[Alice Bob], @game.draw_winners!.map(&:name).sort
  end

  test "Reset winners removes the winners" do
    play_out
    @game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_equal %w[Alice Bob], winner_names
    assert_equal [], @game.reset_winners!
    assert_equal [], winner_names
  end

  test "picking winners is refused until the quiz is over, and changes nothing" do
    travel_to BASE
    @game.start!
    assert_nil @game.pick_top_winners!
    assert_nil @game.draw_winners!
    assert_nil @game.reset_winners!
    assert_equal [], winner_names
  end

  test "each winner action changes the revision and the progress, and ticks both streams" do
    play_out
    revision = @game.revision
    progress = @game.progress
    assert_broadcasts(@game.live_stream_name, 1) do
      assert_broadcasts(@game.play_stream_name, 1) { @game.pick_top_winners! }
    end
    @game.reload
    assert_equal revision + 1, @game.revision
    assert_equal progress + 1, @game.progress
  end

  test "the winners count is read from the quiz as it is now" do
    play_out
    assert_equal 2, @game.winners_count
    @quiz.update!(winners_count: 5)
    assert_equal 5, @game.winners_count
  end
end

require "application_system_test_case"

class LatencyProbeTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include GameFixtures

  test "how fast the phones follow the moderator" do
    quiz = build_quiz_with_questions
    visit "/moderate/quizzes/#{quiz.id}"
    click_button "Start a game"
    code = Game.last.code
    using_session(:alice) { visit "/play/#{code}"; fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"; click_button "Join"; assert_text "Hi, Alice!" }
    using_session(:bob) { visit "/play/#{code}"; fill_in "Your name", with: "Bob"; click_button "Join"; assert_text "Hi, Bob!" }
    assert_text "Players: 2"
    times = {}
    t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    click_button "Start"
    using_session(:alice) { assert_text "Question 1 of 3" }
    times[:start_to_alice] = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t
    using_session(:bob) { assert_text "Question 1 of 3" }
    times[:start_to_bob] = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t

    using_session(:alice) { click_button "429" }
    t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    click_button "Finish"
    using_session(:alice) { assert_text "Correct!" }
    times[:finish_to_alice_result] = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t
    click_button "Next"
    t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    click_button "Finish"; click_button "Next"; click_button "Finish"; click_button "End quiz"
    t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    using_session(:alice) { assert_text "The quiz is over" }
    times[:end_to_alice] = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t
    t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    click_button "Top 3"
    using_session(:alice) { assert_text "You won!" }
    times[:top_to_alice_won] = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t
    puts "\nLATENCY " + times.transform_values { |v| (v * 1000).round }.inspect
  end
end
EOF

require "application_system_test_case"

class LayoutProbeTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include GameFixtures

  [ [ 1280, 1000 ], [ 1280, 720 ], [ 390, 844 ] ].each do |width, height|
    test "leaderboard layout #{width}x#{height} with 30 players" do
      quiz = build_quiz_with_questions
      game = Game.create_from_quiz!(quiz)
      questions = game.game_questions.to_a
      players = 30.times.map { |i| game.join("Player number #{i + 1}") }
      game.start!
      players.each_with_index do |player, i|
        game.answer!(player, questions[0].options.find_by(correct: i.even?) || questions[0].options.first)
      end
      game.finish!
      game.end_quiz!
      page.driver.browser.resize(width: width, height: height) rescue nil
      page.current_window.resize_to(width, height) rescue nil
      visit "/moderate/games/#{game.id}"
      metrics = page.evaluate_script(<<~JS)
        (() => {
          const list = document.querySelector("ol.leaderboard")
          const bar = document.querySelector(".screen-controls").getBoundingClientRect()
          const r = list.getBoundingClientRect()
          const h1 = document.querySelector("h1.screen__ended").getBoundingClientRect()
          return {
            viewport: [window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight],
            pageScrollH: document.documentElement.scrollHeight,
            listClientH: list.clientHeight, listScrollH: list.scrollHeight,
            listBottom: Math.round(r.bottom), listTop: Math.round(r.top), listRight: Math.round(r.right),
            barTop: Math.round(bar.top), h1Top: Math.round(h1.top),
            items: document.querySelectorAll("li.leader").length,
            overflowX: document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth
          }
        })()
      JS
      puts "\nLAYOUT #{width}x#{height} " + metrics.inspect
      assert_equal 30, metrics["items"]
    end
  end
end
EOF

messages.content: The form has labelled option rows, so I can script the quiz creation through the UI as well. I'll write a standalone Capybara and Cuprite script outside the repo. It creates a quiz through the settings page and two questions, then plays a game against the running production server, with Bob joining first and answering slowest.

arguments.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/e2e && cat > /tmp/e2e/run.rb <<'EOF'
require "capybara"
require "capybara/cuprite"

BASE = "http://localhost:3000"
Capybara.register_driver(:e2e) do |app|
  Capybara::Cuprite::Driver.new(app, browser_path: "/usr/bin/chromium", headless: true,
    process_timeout: 60, timeout: 20, browser_options: { "no-sandbox" => nil, "disable-dev-shm-usage" => nil })
end
Capybara.default_driver = :e2e
Capybara.app_host = BASE
Capybara.run_server = false
Capybara.default_max_wait_time = 5

SESSIONS = {}
def session(name)
  SESSIONS[name] ||= Capybara::Session.new(:e2e)
end

def moderator
  s = session(:mod)
  s.driver.browser.network.authorize(user: "moderator", password: "s3cret-pass") { |req| req.continue }
  s
end

def clock = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)

mod = moderator
mod.visit "/moderate/quizzes/new"
mod.fill_in "Title", with: "Production check"
mod.fill_in "Number of winners", with: "2"
mod.click_button "Save quiz"
mod.click_link "Settings"
puts "settings winners field = #{mod.find_field('Number of winners').value}"
mod.visit "/moderate"
mod.click_link "Production check"

[ [ "Which is faster?", "Fast", "Slow" ], [ "Which is bigger?", "Big", "Small" ] ].each do |text, right, wrong|
  mod.click_button "Add question"
  mod.fill_in "Question", with: text
  mod.fill_in "Option 1", with: right
  mod.fill_in "Option 2", with: wrong
  mod.check "Option 1 is correct"
  mod.click_button "Save question"
end

mod.click_button "Start a game"
code = mod.find(".lobby__url").text[%r{/play/(\w+)\z}, 1]
puts "code=#{code}"

join = lambda do |name|
  s = session(name.downcase.to_sym)
  s.visit "/play/#{code}"
  s.fill_in "Your name", with: name
  s.click_button "Join"
  s.assert_text "Hi, #{name}!"
end
join.call("Bob")
join.call("Alice")
join.call("Carol")
mod.assert_text "Players: 3"

t0 = clock
mod.click_button "Start"
mod.assert_text "Question 1 of 2"
session(:alice).assert_text "Which is faster?"
puts "start -> phone question: #{((clock - t0) * 1000).round} ms (incl. click)"

session(:alice).click_button "Fast"
sleep 1.5
session(:bob).click_button "Fast"
session(:carol).click_button "Slow"
mod.click_button "Finish"
mod.click_button "Next"
session(:alice).assert_text "Which is bigger?"
session(:alice).click_button "Big"
session(:bob).click_button "Big"
session(:carol).click_button "Small"
mod.click_button "Finish"
mod.click_button "End quiz"

mod.assert_text "The quiz is over"
mod.assert_selector "li.leader", count: 3
puts "leaderboard: " + mod.all("li.leader").map { |li| li.text.gsub(/\s+/, " ").strip }.inspect

session(:alice).assert_text "Place 1 of 3"
session(:bob).assert_text "Place 2 of 3"
puts "alice: " + session(:alice).find(".result-card").text.gsub(/\s+/, " ")
puts "bob:   " + session(:bob).find(".result-card").text.gsub(/\s+/, " ")

t1 = clock
mod.click_button "Top 2"
session(:alice).assert_text "You won!"
session(:bob).assert_text "You won!"
puts "top 2 -> phones: #{((clock - t1) * 1000).round} ms"
session(:carol).assert_no_text "You won!"
puts "winners on screen: " + mod.all("li.leader .leader__badge").size.to_s

mod.click_button "Reset winners"
mod.assert_no_selector "li.leader .leader__badge"
session(:alice).assert_no_text "You won!"
puts "reset ok"
mod.click_button "Draw"
mod.assert_selector "li.leader .leader__badge", count: 2
puts "draw ok: " + mod.all("li.leader .leader__badge").size.to_s
puts "E2E DONE"
EOF
cd /app && env -u RAILS_ENV BROWSER_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium timeout 600 bundle exec ruby /tmp/e2e/run.rb 2>&1 | tail -40
