cd /app && cat > docs/prizes.md <<'EOF'
# Prizes: scoring, the leaderboard and the winners

The design notes for what happens after **End quiz**. The live game itself (phases,
buttons, live updates) is in `live-game.md`; the general notes in `design-notes.md`.

## Scoring

- **Each correct answer gives one point.** A question may have several correct
  options; any correct pick gives its one point. Only the **last pick** of a question
  counts, as before.
- **Speed.** The time of an answer runs from the moment its question opened
  (`game_questions.opened_at`, set on the server when the moderator clicks Start or
  Next) to the player's last pick (`answers.picked_at`). Each pick stamps `picked_at`,
  even when the option stays the same, because `updated_at` does not move then.
  A player's speed is the **total** of the times of their **correct** answers, in whole
  microseconds (`players.speed_micros`). Only the server's clock is used.
- **Ranking** (`Leaderboard.rank`): more points first. Equal points: the lower total
  speed wins. Still equal: the player who joined first wins, so places are always
  distinct and numbered 1..n.
- **Players see no points or places during the game.** Points and places appear only
  after the end. Phones show "Correct!" or "Wrong!" per question, as before. That says
  nothing about the points.

## When the results are stored

`Game#end_quiz!` ranks the players inside the same transaction as the move to `ended`,
and stores `points`, `speed_micros` and `place` on each player. After that, answers are
refused (`answer!` checks the phase inside its transaction), so the stored result cannot
go stale. It is stored rather than recomputed because every phone fetches its place on
each tick, and the ranking would otherwise be redone for every phone.

## Winners

Chosen by the moderator on the big screen, **after the end only**. Before the end,
\"Top N\", \"Draw\" and \"Reset winners\" are refused with \"The winners are picked after
the quiz is over.\"

- **Top N** (the button reads "Top 3" for 3 winners): the first N places that have
  points.
- **Draw** (ties): everyone with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining
  prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points.
  Speed does not count there. Each click draws again and replaces the previous winners.
- **Players with 0 points never win**, with either button. If fewer than N players have
  points, all of them win. If nobody has points, nobody wins and the moderator is told
  "No player has points, so nobody wins."
- **Reset winners** clears every winner.

N is `quizzes.winners_count`, read from the quiz at each click (`Game#winners_count`),
not copied when the game starts. So a change in the quiz settings applies until the
winners are picked. This is a deliberate choice: the moderator who changes the number
expects it to count at the moment they pick.

Each winner action runs in one transaction, so the screens and phones get the same
result. It bumps `revision` (big screen) and `progress` (phones), and ticks both
streams. Measured against `bin/serve` (solid_cable), a phone shows a new winner about
130 ms after the click.

## The settings field

- **Number of winners**: a whole number from 1 to 1000 (`Quiz::MAX_WINNERS_COUNT`).
  The cap keeps the value inside the integer column. Default 3. Shown under Title on
  the quiz form, which serves both "New quiz" and "Settings".
- The JSON export does not include it: the export keys are a fixed format (see
  `quiz-json-format.md`). An imported quiz gets the default 3.

## Screens

- **Big screen, after End quiz.** "The quiz is over", then the leaderboard: one
  `li.leader` per player, in order. Each row has the place, the name, the points
  ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points") and, for winners only, a "Winner" badge
  (`.leader.is-winner`, `.leader__badge`). The controls bar offers "Top 3" (the
  current N), "Draw" and "Reset winners".
- **Layout.** On a wide screen (901 px and up) the list scrolls inside the screen, so
  it never runs under the fixed controls bar (checked at 1280x720 and 1280x1000). On a
  narrow screen the title sits above the list, the page scrolls, and the bottom padding
  keeps the last rows clear of the wrapped controls bar (checked at 390x844).
- **Phone, after End quiz.** "The quiz is over", then "Place 2 of 5" and "3 points".
  A winner also sees a "You won!" banner. A browser that never joined sees only "The
  quiz is over": no place and no points.

## Decisions to keep

- Places are sequential (1, 2, 3...). A full tie is broken by who joined first, so no
  two players share a place.
- The "last pick" time includes the phone's latency: a tap is timed when the server
  receives it. The server's clock is the only clock used.
- Draw and Reset winners have no `confirm()`. Nothing is deleted: a winner can be
  picked again at once.

## Labels the QA tests rely on

"Number of winners" (field, Settings and New quiz), "Top 3" (button, shows N),
"Draw", "Reset winners", "Winner" (badge on a leaderboard row), "You won!" (phone),
"Place 2 of 5" and "3 points" (phone), "2 points" / "1 point" / "0 points"
(leaderboard rows).

## Code

- `app/models/leaderboard.rb`: `Leaderboard` (plain Ruby): `rank`, `answer_micros`,
  `top`, `draw`. No database access.
- `app/models/game.rb`: `rank_players!` (inside the end move), `pick_top_winners!`,
  `draw_winners!`, `reset_winners!`, `ranked_players`, `winners_count`.
- `app/models/quiz.rb`: the `winners_count` rule. `app/models/player.rb`: the result
  columns.
- `app/controllers/moderate/games_controller.rb`: `top_winners`, `draw_winners`,
  `reset_winners`, and the messages.
- Views: `moderate/games/_screen.html.erb` (ended branch and controls),
  `play/_state.html.erb` (ended branch), `moderate/quizzes/_form.html.erb` (field).
- Styles: `game.css` (leaderboard scrolling, the badge next to the name).
- Migration: `db/migrate/20261125020000_add_prizes.rb`.

## Tests

- `test/models/leaderboard_test.rb`: ranking, speed, last pick, Top N, Draw, the
  tie rules, zero points, draws again on each call. No database.
- `test/models/game_prizes_test.rb`: stored results after End quiz (travelled time),
  the last pick, winner actions, refusals before the end, the broadcasts.
- `test/models/quiz_test.rb`: the winners count rule and its message.
- `test/integration/prizes_test.rb`: the field, the leaderboard, the buttons and their
  login, the refusals, the phones (place, points, "You won!"), ETags.
- `test/system/prizes_test.rb`: a whole game in four browsers with real time: Bob joins
  first and answers slower, and speed puts Alice first. Winners appear live.
EOF

messages.content:
The work is complete and verified. Here's the state of the repo before I submit.

Summary of what I built, on top of the existing live-game code (which was already uncommitted in the working tree; I left all changes uncommitted):

**Settings:** "Number of winners" field (whole number, 1–1000, default 3) on the quiz form. Errors read naturally, e.g. "Number of winners must be greater than or equal to 1".

**Scoring:**
- One point per correct answer. Only the last pick counts.
- Each pick stamps `answers.picked_at`, because `updated_at` doesn't change when a player re-taps the same option.
- Speed is the total time of correct answers, from question open to last pick, using the server clock only.
- Ranking: points, then lower speed, then join order.
- Results are stored once, inside the "End quiz" transaction. Answers are refused after that, so the stored results can't go stale.

**Leaderboard:** the big screen lists one `li.leader` per player, with place, name, and "N points", plus a "Winner" badge for winners. Phones show "Place N of M", "N points", and "You won!" for winners. Nothing about points or places appears before the end.

**Winners:** "Top 3" (N from the quiz setting), "Draw", and "Reset winners" are available only after the end. Zero-point players never win. Draw keeps everyone above the N-th place and fills the rest at random from the tied group, ignoring speed, and each click redraws. Every change ticks both the big screen and the phones.

**Live timing:** measured in browsers, phones follow the moderator in about 120–160 ms. This includes a production run against `bin/serve` with solid_cable.

**Verification:**
- 191 unit and integration tests, and 31 system tests, all passing. That includes a new whole-game browser test where the faster player beats an earlier joiner on speed.
- Rubocop and brakeman are clean, and the bundle resolves offline.
- A fresh production boot played a full game through the real server.

**Decisions you may want to review** (all documented in `docs/prizes.md`):
- N is read from the quiz at each pick, not copied when the game starts, so a settings change applies until the winners are picked.
- The JSON export format is unchanged, so the winners number isn't exported. An imported quiz gets 3.
- I capped the number at 1000. Without a cap, `99999999999` passed validation and would overflow the integer column on save.
- Layout: on wide screens the leaderboard scrolls inside the screen. On narrow ones the page scrolls. I checked both by measuring the DOM.

Docs updated: new `docs/prizes.md`, plus `live-game.md`, `design-notes.md`, `quiz-json-format.md`, and the README.
